 Lafourche Parish 2026 property tax bills now available, deadline set for Dec. 31 
 By TYLER ESCHETTE
Gazette Writer 
 Tyler Eschette 
 Gazette Writer

 Lafourche Parish property owners should begin receiving their 2026 property tax statements, with the Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Office announcing that bills have been mailed and are now available to view and pay online.
 Sheriff Craig Webre announced that property owners can access their tax statements and make payments through the Sheriff’s Office website at LPSO.net/PayMyTaxes .
 Property taxes help fund a variety of public services throughout Lafourche Parish, including roads, drainage, levees, law enforcement, fire departments, hospitals, ambulance services, schools and recreation.
 According to the LPSO, all property tax payments are due by Thursday, Dec. 31. Under state law, delinquent taxes accrue interest at a rate of 1% per month until paid, in addition to the costs associated with delinquent collections.
 Property owners have several options for paying their tax bills. According to the LPSO, payments can be made online at LPSO.net/PayMyTaxes using a debit card, credit card, PayPal, Venmo or electronic check.
 Payments may also be mailed using the envelope provided with the tax statement. However, the LPSO cautions property owners that using the provided envelope after Dec. 31 could result in delayed payment and penalties.
 Residents can make payments by phone by calling 985-449-4430 and selecting Option 1 for the payment center.
 In-person payments are accepted from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding weekends and holidays at the following LPSO locations:
 • Administrative Office : 200 Canal Boulevard, Thibodaux
 • Criminal Operations Center: 805 Crescent Ave., Lockport
 • South Lafourche Substation: 102 West 91st St., Cut Off
 Property owners who use their bank’s online bill-pay service should make payments payable to the LPSO and send them to:
 Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Office 
 P.O. Box 5608
 Thibodaux, LA 70302
 The LPSO also reminds property owners that they remain responsible for paying their taxes even if they do not receive a statement in the mail. Tax bills may occasionally be sent to a previous property owner or lost during delivery.
 Those with a mortgage are encouraged to check with their mortgage company before making a payment, as property taxes may already be paid through an escrow account, according to the LPSO.
 Unpaid property taxes are subject to tax lien auction, along with additional fees and penalties.
 For more information or to review a tax notice, property owners can visit LPSO.net/PayMyTaxes and search using the format ‘last name, first name.’
 Questions about the amount owed, property assessments or property ownership should be directed to the Lafourche Parish Assessor’s Office at 985-447-7242.
 For questions regarding charges associated with property abatement liens, residents should contact Lafourche Parish Government at 985-532-6229. Residents within the Town of Golden Meadow may call 985-475-5212.
